lede: Singapore is dealing with haze and showers while the government puts S$45 million behind factory AI, Jio's record IPO opens for bidding in India, and Anthropic's compute and policy moves keep making news ahead of its November listing.
stocks_note: Latest completed closes: New York, Tuesday 20 October (AAPL, GOOGL) and SGX, Tuesday 20 October (DBS), via Yahoo Finance. No earnings dates turned up in today's sources.

sections.title: Apple
sections.subtitle: Official news in brief, then 9to5Mac and MacRumors

official.label: From Apple
official.summary: Apple named new American supplier partners for iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, covering critical materials and components, and expanded earlier commitments. It also opened its Designers of Tomorrow showcase with Design Miami in Paris, themed around presence. iPhone Duo pre-orders began on 16 October, and a new Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini landed earlier this month.

items.headline: Apple revokes eight web certificates scammers could abuse, but Macs may still trust them
items.summary: Apple has blocked eight web security certificates that could have let fraudsters pose as genuine websites. A cryptography engineer warns that Macs may keep trusting the compromised certificates, so the underlying weakness has not been closed yet.

items.headline: iPhone Duo review: a compact foldable that changes the iPhone shape
items.summary: The first reviews call the iPhone Duo the biggest change to the iPhone form factor in almost 20 years. It pairs a compact, notebook-style body with an iPad-like inner display. It looks a little awkward, but the reviewer says there are good reasons for that.

items.headline: Loop Capital drops Apple to Hold on weaker iPhone outlook
items.summary: The analyst firm cut Apple from Buy to Hold, arguing the company is unlikely to recover an estimated 13 million iPhone units trimmed from its second-half 2026 plans. The call is relayed through an Investing.com report.

items.headline: UK regulator proposes easing the way for Apple Pay rivals
items.summary: The Competition and Markets Authority wants changes that would make it easier and cheaper for other companies to offer payment options on the iPhone. The proposals take aim at Apple's fees and the way access to the phone's tap-to-pay hardware is handled.

items.headline: Why Singapore finds it hard to pin haze fires on specific companies
items.summary: Enforcement of the haze law is held back by cross-border investigations and the difficulty of gathering evidence. Experts discuss how the law could be strengthened as smoke from the region returns to Singapore skies this week.

items.headline: MOH releases its N95 mask stockpile to help retailers meet haze demand
items.summary: The Ministry of Health has opened up its stock of N95 or equivalent masks so retailers can keep up with public demand during the haze. Pet owners are also seeing effects, with some vets reporting up to 15 per cent more eye and breathing cases.

items.headline: COE premiums climb again in first tender after the system review was announced
items.summary: Category A closed at S$132,004 and Category B at S$131,901. The Land Transport Authority says demand stays high ahead of an upcoming car exhibition, so buyers should not expect quick relief.

items.headline: Singapore adds S$135 million for coastal protection and flood research
items.summary: The new money builds on the S$125 million used in 2023 to set up the Coastal Protection and Flood Management Research Programme. It extends work on defending a low-lying island against rising seas and heavier rain.

items.headline: Police: at least S$83,000 lost to fake Simba telco websites since March
items.summary: Scammers bought sponsored search results that impersonated the telco, leading victims to fake sites. Police urge people to type official addresses directly instead of clicking top search ads.

items.headline: Jio Platforms opens bidding for a US$3.2 billion IPO
items.summary: The listing is expected to be an offer for sale, so existing investors sell shares and Jio raises no new capital. It is billed as India's biggest public offering and is being watched as a test of appetite for large tech issues.

items.headline: SBI admits customer data was exposed on the dark web
items.summary: State Bank of India has acknowledged that some customer data surfaced on the dark web, according to The Hindu's top news roundup. Details on scale and cause are still emerging.

items.headline: Delhi Police seek a three-day custody extension for two CJP leaders
items.summary: The two were remanded to judicial custody on 14 October after being detained for allegedly entering the denotified Jantar Mantar protest site. They later withdrew their High Court plea against the extension.

items.headline: Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat sleeper may launch on 1 November
items.summary: The 16-coach train, built for up to 160 kmph, could cut the journey from about 24 hours to 16. Fares are reported to range from Rs 2,600 to Rs 4,250.

items.headline: Tamil Nadu on alert as a new Bay of Bengal system keeps heavy rain going until 26 October
items.summary: The regional weather centre expects intense rainfall to persist, with warnings issued to residents along the Palar river and a school holiday declared in Chennai. The state is also repairing rainwater harvesting structures ahead of the northeast monsoon.

items.headline: Russia frees US citizen Stephen Hubbard as a Trump envoy meets Putin
items.summary: The 74-year-old former teacher was released with no prisoner swap required, according to Trump. The release came as the envoy held talks with the Russian president.

items.headline: France argues over who is to blame for some of its worst urban unrest in decades
items.summary: Cost-of-living protests turned into riots in several cities, with Apple stores among the businesses looted. Macron says Trump spread rumours about the protests, while analysts disagree on the causes.

items.headline: Musk confirms Tesla and SpaceX are weighing a merger
items.summary: Special committees at both companies have been set up to study a possible mega-merger. No terms or timetable have been announced.

items.headline: Sudan army drone strikes reportedly kill more than 300 people
items.summary: Sources say drones hit a truck carrying people to a funeral and a market alleged to supply fuel to the RSF. The toll comes from unconfirmed accounts.

items.headline: Iran's enriched uranium resurfaces as a sticking point in talks with the US
items.summary: Enrichment has become a major point of contention as diplomats push to end the war. Both sides are still negotiating the terms.

brief.summary: Enterprise Singapore will put more than S$45 million over three years into helping smaller manufacturers adopt ready-made AI tools, announced at ITAP 2026. At Cyber Week, K Shanmugam asked AI companies for full and immediate transparency when incidents occur, and OpenAI backed the idea. Separately, NTU was ranked first globally in AI in a new university ranking.

sections.title: Singapore AI startups
sections.subtitle: Funding, hiring, and what they're building

items.headline: Genie Health, from PropertyGuru's former CEO, raises US$3 million seed
items.summary: The AI health startup aims to personalise healthcare. Investors include Liminal, the Temasek-backed venture studio.

items.headline: Manus reportedly secures more than US$500 million
items.summary: One AI news tracker says the Singapore-based agent startup raised the round in the week to 12 October, led by Boyu Capital and IDG Capital, with Tencent, HSG and ZhenFund joining. It rests on a single source, so treat it as unconfirmed.

items.headline: TeamSolve raises US$2.5 million seed for industrial AI
items.summary: The Singapore startup builds AI solutions for industrial and utilities operators. The deal appeared in DealStreetAsia's early-October Southeast Asia roundup.

items.headline: Moonshot AI, maker of Kimi, appears to be setting up in Singapore
items.summary: A new sales role listed on the company's LinkedIn page as of 20 October points to a Singapore operation, Business Times reports. It is an early sign the Chinese AI lab wants a regional commercial presence.

items.headline: Anthropic opens its Singapore office and lists nine local roles
items.summary: The new Raffles Place office is its fifth in Asia-Pacific. Openings span applied AI, finance, marketing, sales and economic research, and the company signed a safety agreement with the government.

items.headline: Anthropic pitches an AI safety bill with a judge-approval step
items.summary: The proposal would let regulators stop a model only if a court agrees, even where it could cause 50 or more deaths. Critics say it looks protective but limits what agencies can actually do.

items.headline: Anthropic's cloud partnerships are reportedly getting messy before its November IPO
items.summary: Cloud providers increasingly see the company as a competitor, and it is said to be struggling to secure enough compute while its infrastructure bill balloons.

items.headline: OpenAI buys Orchestra Bio to build out its life-sciences work
items.summary: The team and technology will join Rosalind, OpenAI's model for life-sciences research, and its Rosalind Workbench tool for planning experiments and analysing results.

items.headline: Google joins Amazon in helping PyTorch developers leave Nvidia GPUs
items.summary: Google released a tool that makes it easy to move PyTorch apps off Nvidia hardware, following a similar move by Amazon. Both are aimed at Nvidia's hold on AI developers.

items.headline: OpenAI will sell its top models on Google Cloud
items.summary: The deal puts OpenAI's best models in front of Google Cloud's enterprise customers, the latest step in its push into corporate sales.

items.headline: DeepSeek open-sources an internal framework for running models cheaply
items.summary: The start-up released the tool in full, and a senior researcher described a growing divide between open-source and closed-source AI, saying the aim is a total victory for open models.

items.headline: China sets up a state-owned firm in Xiongan to manage national data for AI
items.summary: The new enterprise will develop the country's large data resources, a move meant to speed up the AI industry and strengthen the digital economy.

items.headline: Hacker Yuki Chen joins Chinese AI leader Z.ai
items.summary: The prolific security researcher's move comes as China's AI sector grapples with the technology's growing effect on cyberspace.

items.headline: Alibaba says chips using its RISC-V design have shipped more than 6 billion units
items.summary: Damo Academy's XuanTie architecture is now a base for the group's push into AI and automotive chips.

items.headline: Apec finance ministers agree on cooperation over AI and digital financing
items.summary: Meeting in Hong Kong, the finance chiefs reached consensus on policy coordination and on financing technology and AI.
